title: Other Mac handoff 1: Kev first pass on every registered study
description:
**This epic is your whole assignment.** You were given only this epic's ID. Do every child task below, in order, one at a time, then close the epic.

**Job:** run Kev (the pinned local model) over the first-pass, 500-item-per-cell subsample of every study registered in the Kev amendments: 21 runs, 122,438 requests, about 3.1 hours on a quiet Mac. Each child task names its manifest under `docs/kev-runs/<study>/` and the answer folder it writes.

## Read first
- `kbs show BD-dd780c`: the runbook (one-time setup, the server, the exact collect command, returning data). Follow it. Where a child task names a different manifest path than the runbook's example, the child task wins.
- This repository uses Git Flow: work from `develop`, pull it before each task, never push to `main`.

## How to work through it
1. Do the one-time setup from the runbook if this Mac has not (venv, model snapshots).
2. Start the pinned Kev server **once** and leave it up for the whole epic; stop it after the last task or if you must stop.
3. For each child, in order: `kbs show <child id>`; run `python -m scripts.run_kev_study collect --manifest <the child's manifest>` with the runbook's identity flags (it resumes if interrupted); when it prints `"complete": true`, commit only the finished files it wrote (`answers/kev/<task>/*.jsonl.gz` and `*.metadata.json`, never `*.partial.jsonl`) to branch `runs/<child id>` and push that branch.
4. Back on `develop`: comment the request count and any error on the child, close it, `kbs commit`, `git pull --rebase origin develop`, `git push origin develop`. Merge your `runs/` branch into `develop` and push `develop` too.
5. If a child fails, comment the error on it, leave it open, and go on to the next. Do not retry more than once.

## Rules
- One heavy job at a time on this machine. No `bd replay`, no test suite, no site build here.
- Kev only. Do not touch Laya or Jev, and never touch `project/` directly.

## Order and why
1. `architect-interior-designer` (batch2-veteran-sexuality): 3 cells, 4,500 requests

comments.text: Message for the agent on the other Mac. Every run in this epic must be the CAPPED first pass, never a full run. Each manifest under docs/kev-runs/<study>/ has "item_cap": 500 on every cell and states the exact request count; run_kev_study collect --manifest <that file> honours it and prints the total. Check before you start each task: the requests count it plans must equal the number in the child issue title (for example architect batch-2 is 4,500 requests, 1,500 per cell; the full registered size would be 3,213 per cell, which is NOT what we want). If it plans more than the title says, stop, do not answer anything, and comment here. Do not use docs/kev-coverage-*.json (those are the full, uncapped registrations) and do not remove item_cap. Your architect batch-2 data (BD-e7fdc9) is correct: 1,500 rows per cell, matching its manifest. Please reply here with (1) which manifest and request count you are running right now and (2) if you have started anything that is larger than its title, what it is and how far it got. Keep going in order otherwise.
